# yaac

**Yet Another APRS Client — the deep, portable Java one**

- **Version recorded:** build-230
- **Categories:** `packet`, `tracking`
- **Upstream:** <https://www.ka2ddo.org/ka2ddo/YAAC.html>
- **Needs first:** `default-jre-headless`, `libjssc-java`

## What it does

A full APRS station in Java: maps with offline OSM tiles, digipeater and I-gate operation, messaging, weather station support, and a plugin system -- portable across anything with a JRE.

## Why you would want it

Between Xastir's mapping focus and QtBPQAPRS's messaging focus, YAAC is the do-everything option, and the one with first-class digipeater and I-gate roles. KA2DDO maintains it actively and documents it deeply.

## Before it will work

A TNC (Direwolf serves well -- this catalog configures it) or an APRS-IS passcode for internet-only operation. Serial TNCs need the dialout group; libjssc-java supplies the serial bindings.

## How it installs

- prebuilt zip from https://www.ka2ddo.org/ka2ddo/YAAC.zip
  - The zip is loose-rooted (YAAC.jar, lib/, images/, plugins/ at top level) and lands whole under the shared prefix; YAAC reads everything relative to its jar.

## Known problems

Unaffected by Linux 7.1's removal of the kernel AX.25 stack: it speaks KISS and AGW to Direwolf directly. See `docs/reference/kernel-ax25.md`. First run opens a setup wizard; give it a moment on the first tile download. The single-roll pin above means an upstream roll turns into a hash-mismatch refusal until this manifest is re-pinned -- deliberate, and the cadence hint says why.

## Keeping it current

- probe: none
- strategy: reinstall
- Upstream rolls YAAC.zip in place, several times a year, announced on the yaac-users group. A hash mismatch on install IS the update signal; refetch and re-pin.

## Where to get help with the software itself

Andrew KA2DDO; the yaac-users group and an extensive built-in manual.
